title: Protecting Biodiversity
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Protecting Biodiversity Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Explain why biodiversity is important; assess the effects of human activities, invasive species and habitat loss on biodiversity; evaluate ways to protect species, including Indigenous approaches. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Biodiversity)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 science worksheets on why biodiversity matters, species at risk, invasive species and conservation in Ontario. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Habitat loss, pollution and invasive species threaten it; protecting habitats helps.
body_html:
How to think about it

Ecosystems with many species are healthier and recover better from change.

  • Biodiversity gives people food, medicine, clean water and pollination (ecosystem services).
  • Threats: habitat loss, pollution, climate change, invasive species like the emerald ash borer.
  • Protection: parks, planting native species, laws for species at risk, Indigenous stewardship.
Example

Why is the emerald ash borer a problem?

it is invasive

no natural predators

Answer: it kills ash trees

Example

How can people help monarch butterflies?

caterpillars eat only milkweed

Answer: plant milkweed

Common mistakes

  • Thinking extinction only happened to dinosaurs.
  • Thinking any new species is good for an ecosystem.
  • Thinking one person cannot help.

faq.q: What is a species at risk?
faq.a: A species that could disappear from the wild, like the woodland caribou or the Blanding's turtle in Ontario.
A species brought to a new area where it spreads quickly and harms native species.
Plant native plants, keep pets from being released, reduce waste and help clean up natural areas.

items.q: What is a wildlife corridor?
c: a fence that keeps animals in
a strip of habitat that connects separated areas so animals can move between them
items.e: Corridors help populations stay connected.

items.q: Noah learns that oceans provide fish to eat. Which ecosystem service is this?
items.e: Ecosystem services are benefits people get from healthy ecosystems.

items.q: Which human activity most reduces biodiversity?
c: destroying habitats to build roads and cities
items.e: Habitat loss is the biggest threat.

items.q: Which is a major cause of biodiversity loss?
items.e: Living things lose their homes.

items.q: What does 'endangered' mean?

items.e: The woodland caribou is a species at risk in Ontario.

items.q: Why is biodiversity important for ecosystems?

items.e: Many species can fill each role.

items.q: Jayden learns that tree roots hold soil on hillsides. Which ecosystem service is this?

items.q: What is biodiversity?

items.e: More kinds of living things means more biodiversity.

items.q: Sofia learns that forests take in carbon dioxide. Which ecosystem service is this?

items.q: How do invasive species harm biodiversity?
c: They compete with or eat native species and have few predators.
items.e: Purple loosestrife crowds out wetland plants.

items.q: Why should you not release a pet turtle or fish into a pond?
c: It is good for the pond.

items.e: Non-native pets can harm local species.

items.q: Why are bees important for biodiversity?

items.e: Without pollinators, many plants cannot make seeds.

items.q: Ava learns that plants release oxygen. Which ecosystem service is this?
items.e: Ecosystem services are benefits people get from healthy ecosystems.
